modelAnswer: Acid rain is precipitation with pH less than 5.6, formed when acidic oxides dissolve in atmospheric water. Primary sources are sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) from fossil fuel combustion. SO₂ oxidizes to SO₃, which reacts with water: $SO_3 + H_2O \rightarrow H_2SO_4$. Similarly, NOₓ forms nitric acid: $4NO_2 + O_2 + 2H_2O \rightarrow 4HNO_3$. These strong acids dissolve in rainwater, lowering its pH and creating acid rain that damages ecosystems and infrastructure.

keyPoints: Correctly interprets ppb as parts per billion by mass for gases
Sets up conversion: 0.5 ppb = 0.5 parts per 10⁹ parts
Calculates mass of O₃ per kg air = 5 × 10⁻¹⁰ kg or 0.5 μg/kg
Shows proper unit conversion and scientific notation
modelAnswer:
To find the mass of O₃ per kg of air at 0.5 ppb concentration:

ppb (parts per billion) means 0.5 parts of O₃ per 10⁹ parts of air by volume. For gases, this equals 0.5 parts by mass per 10⁹ parts of air.

Mass of O₃ per kg of air = $\frac{0.5 \times 1000 \text{ g}}{10^9}$ = $5 \times 10^{-7}$ g/kg = $5 \times 10^{-10}$ kg/kg

Alternatively: 0.5 ppb = $\frac{0.5}{10^9}$ = $5 \times 10^{-10}$ kg O₃ per kg air, or **0.5 μg/kg** of air.
